voices.note: the anonymous tanna kama of the baraita quoted at 96a.12, so named by the stam at 96a.13

props.gloss_en: Shmuel: the Torah forbade only [the part of the nerve] that is on the kaf
Shmuel: as it says, 'on the kaf of the thigh' (Gen 32:33)
Rav Pappa: [Shmuel's dictum] is [the subject of] a tannaitic dispute
the baraita: if he ate it [whole] and it has no olive-bulk, he is liable
R' Yehuda: [he is not liable] until it has an olive-bulk
the Rabbis' reason: it is a [distinct] creature
and R' Yehuda: 'eating' is written of it
and the Rabbis: that 'eating' is for where it has four or five olive-bulks and he ate one olive-bulk -- he is liable
and R' Yehuda derives that from 'that is on the kaf of the thigh'
and the Rabbis: that [phrase] is needed for Shmuel's [dictum] -- the Torah forbade only what is on the kaf of the thigh
and R' Yehuda: 'the thigh' is written -- [the nerve] of the whole thigh
and the Rabbis: that ['the thigh'] is [the nerve] whose prohibition spreads through the whole thigh
the Rabbis: to exclude the outer one, which [is] not [forbidden] -- but in fact [only] what is on the kaf
this 'kaf' is needed to exclude a bird, which has no kaf
